39. VITAMIN D IN PREGNANCY

•Daily requirement during pregnancy & lactation 6000IU/day.

Maternal/Fetal Complications:

•PTE & SGA.
•LBW.
•Impaired glucose tolerance – ethnic based association.
•P0 C/section (vitamin D < 37.5 => risk of C section).
•Bacterial vaginosis.

Neonatal complications:

•Seizures: major cause is vitamin D deficiency.
⇨Hypocalcemia seizures also due to vitamin D deficiency (25% mother has deficiency).

Skeletal development & Growth:

-25(OH) level in mother => reduced BMD in offspring.

Lung development & immune disorders:

-25 (OH) levels in mother =>
→wheeze + asthma
→bronchiolitis.

Screening for Vitamin D Deficiency in pregnancy:

•no role of universal or selective screening as treatment is safe.
•Testing should be done in women with:
1.Low calcium.
2.Bone pain.
3.GI disease.
4.Alcohol abuse.
5.Previous child with Rickets.
6.Drug intake that vitamin D levels.

Supplementation & Treatment in Pregnancy:

•10ug/day
•cholecalciferol or Ergocalciferol safe.

 

⇨Categories of Vitamin D supplementation:

General:

-All pregnant population.
-10ug, 400 units/ day.
-All women (NICE).

High Risk:

•Obese
•Socially excluded.
•Dark skin
•Reduced sun exposure.

 

1000IU/ day.

Risk of PTE => 800IU/ day + calcium.

Treatment of vitamin D deficiency:

•4 – 6 weeks’ treatment.
•20,000IU Cholecalciferol/ week.
•10,000 IU Ergo twice/ week.
•4 – 6 weeks’ treatment followed by

1000IU/day maintenance dose.

•Very high doses 300,000 – 500,000IU.

Risk of fracture so C/I during pregnancy.
